newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tourists flock to France, Disneyland top draw.
newsitem.headline: Tourists flock to France, Disneyland top draw.

text.p: Tourists are flocking to France in greater numbers than ever before, with Mickey Mouse's European residence the main attraction by far.
France's national tourism federation said on Wednesday business was booming, bolstered by currency trends that have cut the cost of a French holiday for many travellers.

It said over two-thirds of its 170 local offices anticipate that 1997 will be as good or better than 1996, when France's appeal was marred by protests over nuclear tests in the Pacific and bomb attacks on the Paris Metro.
Even so, France was arguably the world's top destination in 1996, drawing 62.4 million visitors, up from 52 million in 1990.

The newspaper Le Figaro said on Wednesday the number of tourists had risen between two and three percent midway into the 1997 summer holiday season, with Germans and Britons topping the list of visitors.
But Le Figaro suggested the visitors liked France more than they do the French. "Our hospitality and quality of service leave something to be desired," it quoted a tourism official as saying.
"It's as if, because of our privileged situation, we don't need to make an effort. Fortunately that mentality is changing," the official said.

Although Europeans make up nearly 90 percent of the tourists in France, the biggest increases are in Asian, eastern European and U.S. visitors encouraged by the dollar's 20 percent surge against the franc so far this year.

The Swiss are the top spenders, leaving the country an average of 20,000 francs lighter, compared with 11,000 francs spent by Japanese visitors and 10,000 by U.S. visitors. The Dutch spent just 762 francs on average.
"A Swiss visitor is worth 25 Dutch," the newspaper said.
The top attractions are Euro Disney's Paris theme park, which drew 11.7 million visitors last year, followed by the Georges Pompidou Centre with 5.9 million, the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.
